pattern.description: About ten cropped user tweets about the product hard-cut every 2-3 frames over roughly one second, each crop slightly offset, settling on one tweet.
pattern.why_premium: Plays over 'loved by over a half million' so the testimonials read as sheer volume of real users; uniform dark theme and tight crops keep a frantic cut rate legible and on-brand.

build_hint.gsap: Timeline of N tweet layers: tl.set(layers[i], {autoAlpha: 1}, i * 0.083).set(layers[i - 1], {autoAlpha: 0}, i * 0.083), each layer with a small random x/y offset; optional gsap.to(wrapper, {y: -30, ease: 'none', duration: 1}) drift; last tweet holds.
build_hint.remotion: <Series> of tweet <Series.Sequence durationInFrames={2}> at 24 fps, each with a fixed small translate offset; wrapper translateY = interpolate(frame, [0, 26], [0, -30]) linear; final Sequence holds.

notes: Camera verdict tilt_up likely reflects offsets between successive tweet crops, not a real camera tilt. Same tweet sequence and same settling tweet as e022: the montage appears to repeat (or e022/e023 overlap). Worth a human check.
